extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry, anabelian geometry, and Inter-universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: A research paper developing the Kummer-theoretic and Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of the (reciprocal of the l-th root of the) theta function at l-torsion points, introducing notions such as mono-theta environments, multiradiality, conjugate synchronization, and modified Θ-links (Θ×μ, Θ×μ_gau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial / Uniradial / Coric algorithms (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: an algorithm is coric if it depends only on input from the mono-analytic core common to all spokes; uniradial if it expresses objects in terms that only make sense within a single spoke; multiradial if it expresses objects from a given spoke in terms of corically constructed objects (i.e., objects that make sense from other spokes) and hence is compatible with simultaneous execution at multiple spokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses: multiradial algorithms allow constructions that make sense simultaneously from multiple spokes and typically require allowing certain indeterminacies; uniradial algorithms may only be executed consistently at a single spoke. Examples and remarks: multiradiality is the desired property for constructing descriptions of 'alien holomorphic structures' (cf. Example 1.7, Remark 1.9.1–1.9.2). Analogy: coric ↔ real-analytic underlying structure; uniradial ↔ holomorphic structure; multiradial ↔ expressing holomorphic objects solely in terms of underlying real-analytic structures (possibly with indeterminacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: A rigidity isomorphism, constructible algorithmically from a mono-theta environment, between (i) the exterior cyclotome (portion of the mono-theta environment arising from roots of unity of the base field) and (ii) an interior cyclotome (a copy of the once-Tate-twisted Galois module Zhat(1)) appearing as a subquotient of the geometric tempered fundamental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: this rigidity isomorphism can be constructed without invoking full local class field theory by using only the torsion subgroup O^μ_{F_v}; it depends essentially on the commutator structure of theta groups. Analogies: corresponds to absence of Zhat^×-power indeterminacies of canonical coordinates or to Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism in p-adic Teichmüller theory. References: Definition 1.1(ii); Proposition 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrete rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Property that one may work with Z-translates of the theta function (i.e., ordinary integer translates) rather than Zhat-translates (profinite completion), so profinite powers of canonical multiplicative coordinates (U) or q-parameters do not occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: avoids having to deal with PD-formal series (the analogues of allowing arbitrary O^hat-powers), making constructions 'non-PD-formal' and compatible with discrete parameter behavior. The paper notes discrete rigidity will be used but plays a less prominent role here (cf. Remark 3.6.5(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant multiple rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: The theta monoid O^×_{F_v} · Θ_v^N (the monoid generated by the reciprocal of the l-th root of the theta function and the unit group of the local ring) admits a canonical splitting up to 2l-th roots of unity determined by evaluation at the 0 (2-torsion) section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: the canonical splitting is algorithmically constructed from the mono-theta environment (Corollary 1.12(ii); Proposition 3.1(i); Proposition 3.3(i)). Analogy: corresponds to uniqueness of canonical coordinates in p-adic Teichmüller theory (no constant multiple indeterminacy). Plays a central role in relation to the log-link in later papers (IUTchIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta monoid and Gaussian monoid (definitions & relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta monoids: monoids generated by the reciprocal of the l-th root of the theta function and local units (O^×_{F_v} · Θ_v^N). Gaussian monoids: monoids arising from evaluation at l-torsion points, e.g., O^×_{F_v} · {q_{v}^{j2}}_{j=1,...,(l-1)/2}. Both admit etale-like and Frobenius-like (Frobenioid-theoretic) versions that must be related via Kummer theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper studies passage from theta monoids to Gaussian monoids via Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation at l-torsion points. Gaussian monoids do not admit a multiradial formulation on their own; multiradiality for Gaussian monoids requires combining with the log-link (IUTchIII). Kummer isomorphisms relate the etale-like and Frobenius-like versions (see Proposition 3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer isomorphism between etale-like and Frobenius-like versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of a Kummer isomorphism that relates etale-like (Galois-theoretic, arithmetic fundamental group) and Frobenius-like (Frobenioid-theoretic, monoidal) versions of theta/gaussian monoids and their unit portions; e.g., relates the unit portion with its Galois action G_v ⋉ O^×_{F_v} to the Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role: essential to relate Frobenius-like and etale-like structures and to carry out evaluation compatibly with Kummer theory. Appears in Proposition 3.3(i) and related discussions. Ensures that evaluation operations compatible with Kummer theory arise from restrictions to Galois sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of Galois evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement of compatibility with Kummer theory forces any 'evaluation operation' (such as evaluating theta at l-torsion points) to arise from restriction to Galois sections of the arithmetic tempered fundamental groups involved (i.e., Galois sections coming from rational points like l-torsion points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization: essentially a tautology emphasized in the paper; relates the evaluation constructions to Galois/section phenomena and to the Section Conjecture context. Used to motivate the form of evaluation and its relation to anabelian reconstruction (e.g., SemiAnbd). See Remarks 1.12.4 and 3.6.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate synchronization (requirements and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections of 'symmetrizing isomorphisms' between the various copies of local absolute Galois groups G_v (and related objects like monoids) at labels in |F_l| at which theta is evaluated. These isomorphisms must be completely well-defined without conjugacy indeterminacies and must arise from a group action (the F_l^{3,±}-symmetry) and from conjugation operations inside a certain arithmetic tempered fundamental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessity: if conjugacy indeterminacies are allowed (i.e., outer isomorphisms), one must sacrifice either distinctness of labels or compatibility with Kummer theory. Consequence: conjugate synchronization enables construction of coric F^{3}_×μ-prime-strips and is crucial for the Θ×μ and Θ×μ_gau-link constructions. See Corollaries 3.5(i), 3.6(i), 4.5(iii), 4.6(iii) and Remark 3.8.3(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that symmetrizing isomorphisms arise from a group action
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinatorial/structural requirement: symmetrizing isomorphisms used in conjugate synchronization must arise from a group action (specifically the F_l^{3,±}-symmetry) so that they satisfy compatibility conditions (e.g., commuting where required) and preserve label distinctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is used to ensure the isomorphisms are free of conjugacy indeterminacies and to permit simultaneous execution across spokes; it is emphasized that at a combinatorial level the F_l^{2}-symmetry is multiradial while the F_l^{3,±}-symmetry is uniradial (see discussion around Fig. I.4 and I.5 and Remarks 4.7.3–4.7.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aut(G_v)- and Zhat^×-indeterminacies (recognition and compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local data such as the topological group G_v and the monoid O^×_{F_v}/O^μ_{F_v} must be regarded as known only up to isomorphism and up to automorphisms coming from Aut(G_v) and Zhat^× actions; these indeterminacies are intrinsic to modified Θ-link constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: the theory must account for these indeterminacies; however, canonical splittings and cyclotomic rigidity depend only on torsion O^μ_{F_v}, which maps to the identity in O^×_{F_v}/O^μ_{F_v} and hence are immune to those indeterminacies (this fact underlies multiradiality of mono-theta-theoretic rigidity properties; see Corollaries 1.10, 1.12; Proposition 3.4(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-theta environment (construction & equivalences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mono-theta environments: Kummer-theoretic data from extracting N-th roots of theta trivializations on Tate curves over mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local fields. They can be constructed either group-theoretically from the tempered fundamental group of the once-punctured elliptic curve or category-theoretically from the tempered Frobenioid determined by line bundles and divisors over tempered coverings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important equivalence: the isomorphism between the two constructions is a kind of Kummer isomorphism for mono-theta environments (cf. [EtTh], Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 5.10(iii)). The mono-theta environment satisfies the three rigidity properties (cyclotomic, discrete, constant multiple rigidity) which drive later constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ×μ-link and Θ×μ_gau-link (definitions & properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Θ×μ-link: a modification of the Θ-link of IUTchI replacing F^3-prime-strips by F^3_×μ-prime-strips (i.e., replacing local O^× by O^×/O^μ). Θ×μ_gau-link: further replaces theta monoids in the Θ×μ-link by Gaussian monoids via an isomorphism coming from Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: these modified links preserve F^3_×μ-prime-strips up to isomorphism and are summarized in Theorems A, B (abbreviated forms of Corollaries 4.10, 4.11). Analogy: passage from Θ×μ to Θ×μ_gau via evaluation corresponds to passing from MF^∇-objects to Galois representations in p-adic Teichmüller analogy. See Corollary 4.10 and surrounding discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation at l-torsion points (theta values shape and indeterminacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating the reciprocal of the l-th root of the theta function at l-torsion points (possibly shifted by a 2-torsion) produces 'theta values at l-torsion points' which, up to 2l-th roots of unity, take the form q_{v}^{j2} for j in {0,1,...,(l−1)/2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values form the building blocks of Gaussian monoids and are central to the analogy with Gaussian distributions and to the construction of Θ×μ_gau-links. The evaluation is subject to Kummer compatibility and the 2l-th-root-of-unity ambiguity; canonical splittings reduce some indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality of mono-theta-theoretic rigidity properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that canonical splittings via evaluation at the zero section and the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism are compatible with (i.e., left unchanged by) Aut(G_v)- and Zhat^×-indeterminacies because only the torsion subgroup O^μ_{F_v} is relevant to their construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: this formal observation is the substantive content of multiradiality for constant multiple/cyclotomic rigidity and is used heavily in proofs across the series (Corollaries 1.10, 1.12; Proposition 3.4(i); implications in IUTchIII). It explains why certain constructions are immune to the global indeterminacies present in Θ-links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaussian monoids do not admit standalone multiradial formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: unlike theta monoids, Gaussian monoids (on their own, as developed in this paper) do not admit a multiradial formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: to obtain a multiradial formulation of Gaussian monoids one must combine the present paper's theory with the log-link theory developed in IUTchIII; the eventual multiradial formulation appears in IUTchIII, Theorem 3.11. See Remarks 2.9.1(iii), 3.4.1(ii), 3.7.1.
